headword: {幕|まく}の{内|うち}{弁当|べんとう}
gloss: traditional boxed lunch with assorted side dishes

definitions.gloss: traditional boxed lunch with assorted side dishes
definitions.explanation: A type of bento box featuring white rice with an assortment of small portions of various side dishes such as grilled fish, egg, vegetables, and pickles. Known for its balanced variety.

examples.japanese: {駅弁|えきべん}の{定番|ていばん}は{幕|まく}の{内|うち}{弁当|べんとう}だ。
examples.english: The classic ekiben is the makunouchi bento.

examples.japanese: {幕|まく}の{内|うち}{弁当|べんとう}はいろいろなおかずが{少|すこ}しずつ{入|はい}っているのが{魅力|みりょく}だ。
examples.english: The appeal of a makunouchi bento is that it contains a little bit of many different side dishes.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{昼食|ちゅうしょく}に{幕|まく}の{内|うち}{弁当|べんとう}を{注文|ちゅうもん}したら、{彩|いろど}りも{味|あじ}もよくて{好評|こうひょう}だった。
examples.english: When I ordered makunouchi bentos for the meeting lunch, they were well received for both their presentation and taste.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
The name comes from {幕|まく}の{内|うち} (between acts), referring to the intermission of kabuki theater performances when these lunches were originally eaten by the audience.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Considered the most standard and representative type of Japanese bento. Common in {駅弁|えきべん} (train station lunches), business catering, and hospital meals. The typical contents include {俵型|たわらがた}のご{飯|はん} (barrel-shaped rice), {焼|や}き{魚|ざかな} (grilled fish), {卵焼|たまごや}き (rolled omelet), {煮物|にもの} (simmered dishes), and {漬|つ}け{物|もの} (pickles).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {幕|まく}の{内|うち}{弁当|べんとう}を{注文|ちゅうもん}する (to order a makunouchi bento)
- {駅弁|えきべん}の{幕|まく}の{内|うち}{弁当|べんとう} (a train station makunouchi bento)
